name: Rebeca Andrade
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in vault and silver in all-around at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held 2021), becoming the first Brazilian female gymnast to win an Olympic medal.
early_history_summary: Andrade began gymnastics at age four after her aunt took her to the gym where she worked in Guarulhos, Brazil. She won the Junior Pan American all-around title at age 13 in 2012 and moved to train at Flamengo in Rio de Janeiro at age 10. Despite three ACL tears (2015, 2017, 2019), she competed at the 2016 Olympics at age 17 and won Olympic gold at 22.
family_context_summary: Born to a single mother, Rosa, one of eight children in Guarulhos, São Paulo. Her mother cleaned houses and walked to work to pay for gymnastics training.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in gymnastics or sports; her aunt worked at a gym and introduced her to the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early physical talent,aunt gym access,Flamengo pipeline,poverty-driven urgency
evidence_summary: Andrade was born into poverty in Guarulhos with a single mother of eight who cleaned houses to fund training. Her aunt's connection to a local gym provided the entry point at age four, and her natural physical talent was evident early — she won the Junior Pan American all-around at 13. She moved to the elite Flamengo club in Rio at age 10, accessing a high-performance pipeline. Three ACL tears before age 22 tested her resilience but she overcame them to win Olympic gold at the 2020 Tokyo Games.
starting_point: Born to a single mother in Guarulhos, São Paulo, one of eight children; mother cleaned houses to pay for gymnastics training.
current_position: Most decorated Brazilian Olympian with six Olympic medals (2 gold, 3 silver, 1 bronze) and nine World Championship medals; continues competing as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won Junior Pan American all-around, vault, and floor exercise gold medals in her international debut.
Competed at the Rio Olympics, placing 11th in the all-around final after recovering from her first ACL tear.
Won Olympic vault gold and all-around silver at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, becoming the first Brazilian female gymnast to medal at an Olympic Games.
Won World Championship all-around gold in Liverpool, becoming the first Brazilian gymnast to win the world all-around title.
Won three golds and four total medals at the World Championships in Antwerp, including vault gold.
Won four Olympic medals at Paris 2024 including floor exercise gold, becoming Brazil's most decorated Olympian.

name: Antonio López García
milestone_by_age_26: Held his first solo exhibition in 1957 in Tomelloso at age 21, and his first solo show in Madrid in 1961 at age 25, establishing him as a leading figure of the New Spanish Realists.
early_history_summary: López García was born in Tomelloso, Spain, months before the Spanish Civil War. His uncle, the painter Antonio López Torres, recognized his early facility for drawing and gave him his first lessons. At age 13 he moved to Madrid to prepare for entrance to the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando, where he studied from 1950 to 1955 and won several prizes. A scholarship in 1955 allowed him to travel to Italy to study Renaissance painting.
family_context_summary: Born to a farming family in Tomelloso, Ciudad Real, Spain, shortly before the Spanish Civil War. His parents were described as 'labradores acomodados' (comfortable farmers).
parent_family_domain_summary: His uncle Antonio López Torres was a local landscape painter who gave him his first art lessons and convinced his parents to send him to Madrid to study.
primary_early_advantage_tags: uncle painter mentor,academy training,peer realist group,postwar isolation
evidence_summary: López García grew up in a farming family in rural Spain during the post-Civil War period. His uncle, a local painter, identified his drawing talent early and provided sustained mentorship, convincing his parents to send him to Madrid at 13. He entered the prestigious Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando at 14, where he won prizes and formed a peer group of realist painters. A scholarship to Italy in 1955 broadened his artistic foundation. His first solo exhibition came at 21 in 1957, and his first Madrid solo show at 25 in 1961.
starting_point: Born to a farming family in Tomelloso, Ciudad Real, Spain, months before the Spanish Civil War; father was a farmer.
current_position: Living in Madrid at age 90; regarded as one of the greatest living realist painters; awarded the Gold Medal for Merit in Fine Arts (1983) and named member of the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando (1993).

trajectory.event: Received a scholarship to travel to Italy and study Renaissance painting after completing studies at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando.
Held his first solo exhibition in Tomelloso, marking the beginning of his public career.
Had his first solo show in Madrid, establishing recognition within the Spanish art world.
Exhibited at the Staempfli Gallery in New York, bringing international recognition.
Received the Gold Medal for Merit in Fine Arts from the Spanish state.
Subject of the film 'El Sol del Membrillo' by Victor Erice, which won the International Critics Prize at Cannes.
Named a full member of the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando.

name: Zbigniew Preisner
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Preisner began writing music for documentaries and short films around 1978 (age 23) but his first feature film score was in 1982 (age 27) and his breakthrough collaboration with Kieślowski came in 1985 (age 30).
early_history_summary: Preisner was born in Bielsko-Biała, Poland, and studied history and philosophy at Jagiellonian University in Kraków. He taught himself music by listening to and transcribing parts from records. He began writing for documentaries and short films around 1978 but did not score a feature film until 1982.
evidence_summary: Preisner was self-taught in music, studying history and philosophy at university. He began writing for documentaries and short films around 1978 (age 23), but his first feature film score was 'Prognoza Pogody' in 1982 (age 27). His breakthrough came with Krzysztof Kieślowski's 'No End' in 1985 (age 30), followed by the acclaimed Dekalog series and Three Colours trilogy. No material, independently verifiable milestone was found at or before age 26.

name: Vera Baboun
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Baboun was an English literature lecturer at Bethlehem University from 1990 onward; her major milestone was becoming the first female mayor of Bethlehem in 2012 at age 48.
early_history_summary: Baboun was born in Bethlehem and earned a master's degree in African-American literature. She lectured in English literature at Bethlehem University from 1990 to 2010 and served as principal of a Catholic high school from 2010 to 2012 before entering politics.
evidence_summary: Baboun's career was primarily academic before her political milestone. She graduated from Bethlehem University in 1985, lectured there from 1990, and became a school principal before being elected mayor of Bethlehem in 2012 at age 48. No material milestone was found at or before age 26.

name: Erwin Wurm
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Wurm was still an art student through 1982 (age 28); his first prize (Otto Mauer Prize) came in 1984 (age 30) and his signature One Minute Sculptures series began in 1996/97.
early_history_summary: Wurm was born in Bruck an der Mur, Austria. His father was a police detective who disapproved of art. He studied art history at the University of Graz (1974-1977), then sculpture at the Mozarteum in Salzburg (1977-1979), and finally at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna (1979-1982). He worked as a freelance artist from the 1980s onward.
family_context_summary: Born in Bruck an der Mur, Styria, Austria; father was a police detective who did not approve of artists. The family lived in a small apartment.
evidence_summary: Wurm developed an interest in art around age 14-15, supported by a teacher. He studied art history, then sculpture at multiple institutions, completing his education in 1982 at age 28. His first recognition (Otto Mauer Prize) came in 1984 at age 30. No material milestone was found at or before age 26.

name: Anne L'Huillier
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. L'Huillier was still a PhD student at age 26; she defended her thesis in 1986 (age 28), obtained a permanent position at CEA the same year, and conducted her groundbreaking high-harmonic generation experiment in 1987 (age 29).
early_history_summary: L'Huillier was born in Paris and studied at elite schools in the Quartier Latin. She was accepted at the École Normale Supérieure in 1977, earned master's degrees in mathematics and physics, and completed a DEA in quantum physics under Claude Cohen-Tannoudji and Serge Haroche. She began her PhD at CEA Saclay but did not defend until 1986.
evidence_summary: L'Huillier had an elite education in Paris (ENS, DEA under Nobel laureates) but was still a PhD student at age 26. Her thesis defense (1986, age 28), permanent CEA position (1986), and groundbreaking high-harmonic generation experiment (1987, age 29) all came after age 26. She won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2023. No material milestone was found at or before age 26.

name: Kurt Wüthrich
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Wüthrich completed his PhD in 1964 at age 26, which is a standard academic degree, not a notable achievement. His pioneering NMR method for protein structure determination came in the 1980s and his Nobel Prize in 2002.
early_history_summary: Wüthrich was born in Aarberg, Switzerland, and grew up in a rural environment. He studied at the University of Bern and began EPR spectroscopy at age 22 in 1960. He completed his PhD at the University of Basel in 1964 under Silvio Fallab, then did postdoctoral work at UC Berkeley and Bell Labs before joining ETH Zurich in 1969.
family_context_summary: Born in Aarberg, Switzerland; father came from a farming family but worked as an accountant. Grew up in a rural environment with interests in natural science.
evidence_summary: Wüthrich began EPR spectroscopy at age 22 and was the first in Switzerland to record EPR spectra of metal complexes in solution, but this was during his PhD studies. He received his PhD in 1964 at age 26 — a standard academic degree, not a notable milestone. His major contribution (NMR method for protein structure determination) came in the 1980s, leading to the 2002 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. No material, independently verifiable milestone was found at or before age 26.

name: Oscar Bonavena
milestone_by_age_26: Defeated rated contender and Canadian champion George Chuvalo at Madison Square Garden on June 23, 1966 (age 23), bringing him to wide public attention; also won the Argentine Heavyweight Title in September 1965 (age 22) and fought Joe Frazier in September 1966 (age 24).
early_history_summary: Bonavena was born in Buenos Aires to Italian immigrants and grew up in the working-class Parque Patricios neighborhood. He had a strong amateur career (lost only once in 46 fights) and competed at the 1963 Pan American Games. He turned professional in February 1964 at age 21 under manager Marvin Goldberg in New York City, quickly racking up knockouts at Madison Square Garden.
family_context_summary: Born in Buenos Aires to Italian immigrant parents; grew up in the working-class Parque Patricios neighborhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class immigrant,46 amateur fights,NYC boxing scene,manager Goldberg
evidence_summary: Bonavena came from a working-class Italian-Argentine family in Buenos Aires. He built an extensive amateur career (46 fights, one loss) before turning professional at 21 in 1964. Under manager Marvin Goldberg, he fought at Madison Square Garden and quickly compiled a knockout streak. He won the Argentine Heavyweight Title at 22 (September 1965) and defeated rated contender George Chuvalo at 23 (June 1966), bringing him to wide public attention. He fought Joe Frazier twice and Muhammad Ali in a notable career, though he never won a world title.
starting_point: Born in Buenos Aires to Italian immigrant parents; grew up in the working-class Parque Patricios neighborhood.
current_position: Died on May 22, 1976 at age 33; shot dead at the Mustang Ranch brothel near Reno, Nevada. Final record: 58 wins, 9 losses, 1 draw.

trajectory.event: Made professional boxing debut in New York City under manager Marvin Goldberg, quickly compiling a string of early knockouts at Madison Square Garden.

Shot and killed at the Mustang Ranch brothel near Reno, Nevada on May 22, 1976.

name: Tan Dun
milestone_by_age_26: His string quartet 'Feng Ya Song' (1982) won second prize at the 1983 Dresden International Weber Chamber Music Competition (age 26), making him the first Chinese-trained composer to win a prize at an international competition for contemporary works.
early_history_summary: Tan Dun was born in a village in Changsha, Hunan, China. During the Cultural Revolution he was sent to work as a rice planter and learned traditional Chinese string instruments. After a ferry accident killed members of a Peking opera troupe, he was recruited as their arranger and violist. In 1977, after passing a highly competitive entrance exam, he entered the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing, where he studied with Zhao Xindao and Li Yinghai and was exposed to Western classical music for the first time.
family_context_summary: Born in 1957 in a village near Changsha, Hunan, China. His mother was a doctor and his father worked at a food research institute before the Cultural Revolution disrupted their lives.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cultural Revolution,rice planter,opera troupe,Central Conservatory,Class of 1978
evidence_summary: Tan Dun grew up in rural Hunan during the Cultural Revolution, when music was discouraged and he was sent to work as a rice planter. He learned traditional instruments in a commune ensemble and was recruited into a Peking opera troupe after a tragic ferry accident. In 1977 he passed the highly competitive entrance exam for the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing, joining the first post-Cultural Revolution class alongside other notable composers. His string quartet 'Feng Ya Song' won second prize at the 1983 Dresden International Weber Competition, making him the first Chinese-trained composer to win at an international contemporary music competition — a milestone at age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1957 in a village near Changsha, Hunan, China; mother was a doctor and father worked at a food research institute before the Cultural Revolution.
current_position: Based in New York City; Dean of the Bard College Conservatory of Music since 2019; Oscar and Grammy-winning composer for 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon' and leading figure in contemporary classical music.

trajectory.event: Passed the highly competitive entrance exam and entered the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing, joining the first post-Cultural Revolution class.

name: Denny Hulme
milestone_by_age_26: Won the New Zealand Gold Star Championship and took a class win at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1961 (age 25), establishing himself as a rising international racing talent after being selected for the New Zealand Driver to Europe scholarship in 1960.
early_history_summary: Hulme was born on a tobacco farm in Motueka, New Zealand, the son of WWII Victoria Cross winner Clive Hulme. He learned to drive trucks as a child, left school to work in a garage, and saved enough to buy an MG TF which he raced in local hillclimbs from 1957. In 1960 he was selected for the New Zealand Driver to Europe scholarship alongside George Lawton, and began racing Formula Junior and F2 in Europe, working as a mechanic in Jack Brabham's garage to make ends meet.
family_context_summary: Born on a tobacco farm in Motueka, New Zealand; father Clive Hulme was a WWII Victoria Cross winner who ran a trucking business after the war. Father helped him buy his first racing car, an MG TF.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a trucking business owner and WWII hero, not from a racing background, but provided access to vehicles and mechanical environment from a young age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: truck driving childhood,garage work,MG TF racing,NZ scholarship,Brabham connection
evidence_summary: Hulme grew up on a New Zealand farm with a trucking business run by his VC-winning father, giving him early access to vehicles and mechanical skills. He left school to work in a garage, saved for an MG TF, and began racing at 21 in 1957. In 1960 he was selected for the prestigious New Zealand Driver to Europe scholarship (previously won by Bruce McLaren), enabling him to race Formula Junior in Europe. He won the NZ Gold Star Championship and a Le Mans class win in 1961 at age 25, working as a mechanic at Brabham's garage to fund his racing. He went on to win the 1967 Formula One World Championship.
starting_point: Born on a tobacco farm in Motueka, New Zealand; father Clive Hulme was a WWII Victoria Cross winner who ran a trucking business.
current_position: Died on October 4, 1992 at age 56; suffered a fatal heart attack while competing in the Bathurst 1000 race. 1967 Formula One World Champion with eight career Grand Prix wins.

trajectory.event: Began racing an MG TF in local hillclimbs and circuit events in New Zealand, winning his first proper race at the New Zealand Grand Prix handicap.
Selected for the New Zealand Driver to Europe scholarship alongside George Lawton, began racing Formula Junior in Europe.
Won the New Zealand Gold Star Championship and took a class win in the 850cc category at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Angus Hyslop.
Made his Formula One debut with Brabham at the Monaco Grand Prix, finishing the season 11th overall.
Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Brabham, becoming the only New Zealander to win the F1 title.
Retired from Formula One after 10 seasons, having won eight Grands Prix.
Died of a heart attack during the Bathurst 1000 touring car race in Australia on October 4, 1992.
